questions.prompt: What does B claim can be sustained within marriage?
questions.promptZh: B认为婚姻内部能维持什么？
options: Only the memory of passion after novelty has necessarily ended.
Novelty and passion, together with spontaneity and even adventure.
Spontaneity only if the partners abandon their first love.
Adventure outside marriage as the sole source of renewed affection.
optionsZh: 新奇必然结束后，只剩激情的记忆。
新奇、激情、自发，甚至冒险感。
只有放弃初恋，自发性才可保持。
婚姻之外的冒险是感情更新的唯一来源。
analyses: A can be sustained包括新奇、激情等，未说新奇必然消失。
B 第一直接句列出这些可能在婚姻内保持的品质，归属是Either/Or中的B。
C first love正是持续更新的对象，非须抛弃的条件。
D within the institution of marriage限定婚内，sole与outside都改了范围。

vocabulary.meaning: 维持；使某状态持续
vocabulary.context: 这里指B认为婚姻内部也可延续新奇与激情，并非一项全体夫妻实验的结论。
vocabulary.example: B argues that a sense of adventure can be sustained within marriage.

questions.evidenceQuote: “B” in Either/Or argues that a sense of novelty, passion, spontaneity, even adventure can be sustained within the institution of marriage, stating that “for me this is a matter of the continual rejuvenation of our first love…. This rejuvenation…is not just a sad backward glance, or the poetic memory of an experience…. This is an activity.” So what is the activity?

questions.prompt: What is the role of the final question about the activity?
questions.promptZh: 末尾追问这种活动是什么，起什么作用？
options: It disputes whether the quoted speaker ever used the word activity.
It turns the discussion into a request for the date of the marriage.
It treats the earlier description as a complete explanation requiring no further detail.
It asks what the previously mentioned activity of rejuvenation actually consists of.
optionsZh: 质疑引述者是否曾用activity一词。
转而询问结婚日期。
把此前描述当作无需补充的完整解释。
追问此前所说更新活动具体包含什么。
analyses: A 紧前引语This is an activity已出现该词，So承接而非否认。
B what is the activity问活动内容，没有日期问题。
C 提问表明尚需说明，不能读成讨论已经结束。
D the activity回指引语并引出具体解释；本问本身尚未给出活动方法。

vocabulary.meaning: 活动；实际进行的过程
vocabulary.context: 此处回指初恋更新的活动，不应仅凭这个词就认定为某种外在运动。
vocabulary.example: The next question asks what the activity consists of.

questions.evidenceQuote: “B” in Either/Or argues that a sense of novelty, passion, spontaneity, even adventure can be sustained within the institution of marriage, stating that “for me this is a matter of the continual rejuvenation of our first love…. This rejuvenation…is not just a sad backward glance, or the poetic memory of an experience…. This is an activity.” So what is the activity?

questions.prompt: In B's description, what makes this thanksgiving an action?
questions.promptZh: 在B的描述中，这种感恩何以算一种行动？
options: It involves an inward wish to hold on to first love.
It requires a publicly observable physical exercise.
It replaces wanting to preserve love with rejecting that love.
It excludes any internal intention from the meaning of action.
optionsZh: 它包含内在保有初恋的愿望。
它要求可公开观察的身体锻炼。
它以拒绝初恋取代保有初恋的愿望。
它把内心意向排除在行动意义之外。
analyses: A not external but internal及to want to hold on给出行动的内在含义；这是B的哲学描述。
B external被明确排除，并没有指定身体训练。
C hold on to表示保有，非拒绝。
D internal正是本句强调的层面，不能删去。

vocabulary.meaning: 保有；努力不失去
vocabulary.context: 在此保有初恋感情，非用手抓住实物。
vocabulary.example: The speaker wants to hold on to the affection of first love.
collocations: hold on to this first love

questions.evidenceQuote: The answer is an internal action, or reflection, including gratitude to God. “A thanksgiving of this kind, like all prayer, is combined with an element of action, not in an external but an internal sense, in this case to want to hold on to this first love.” According to B, grateful reflection in the context of religion helps you maintain your love toward your partner.

questions.prompt: What shift is introduced by the opening question about evidence?
questions.promptZh: 开头询问证据，引入什么转向？
options: From empirical findings to an unrelated account of costume making.
From B's claim to the claim that research is unnecessary.
From a philosophical assertion to asking whether research supports it.
From the nature of first love to the exact age of every participant.
optionsZh: 从实证发现转去不相关的服装制作。
从B的主张转为认定研究不必要。
从哲学主张转向询问有无研究支持。
从初恋性质转去每位参与者精确年龄。
analyses: A 紧后Fincham研究承接证据问题，未转向服装。
B any evidence是询问支持，不是排斥研究。
C assertion指B先前的主张，下一句引研究，构成主张—证据的过渡。
D 当前片段没有给出全体精确年龄，提问中心是主张的支持。

vocabulary.meaning: 主张；有待证据支持的断言
vocabulary.context: 这里指B关于初恋可持续更新的说法，不能把assertion本身等同已经证实。
vocabulary.example: The author asks whether evidence supports the assertion.

questions.evidenceQuote: Is there any evidence for B’s assertion about the continual rejuvenation of first love? Frank Fincham and colleagues did a fascinating study on prayer in the context of romantic relationships. In one study, participants who were currently in an exclusive romantic relationship were recruited. One group of participants was randomly assigned into the prayer condition.

questions.prompt: What was the focus of Fincham and colleagues' study as introduced here?
questions.promptZh: 此处介绍的Fincham及同事研究以什么为焦点？
options: The accuracy of married couples' memories of childhood costumes.
Prayer within romantic relationships.
The musical tempo preferred by retired judges.
The effects of random assignment on participants' religious identities alone.
optionsZh: 已婚伴侣对童年服装记忆的准确度。
恋爱关系情境中的祈祷。
退休法官偏爱的音乐节奏。
仅研究随机分组对宗教身份的影响。
analyses: A 共同故事出现在后面的论述，非该研究的介绍。
B on prayer in the context of romantic relationships明确给对象与情境。
C 音乐是另一处哲学比喻，不是Fincham的研究题目。
D 随机分配是安排条件的方法，当前并未把宗教身份变化定作唯一结果。

vocabulary.meaning: 情境；某事所处的背景
vocabulary.context: 这里限定研究把祈祷放在恋爱关系中考察，不代表研究所有生活领域的祈祷。
vocabulary.example: The study considers prayer in the context of romantic relationships.

questions.evidenceQuote: Is there any evidence for B’s assertion about the continual rejuvenation of first love? Frank Fincham and colleagues did a fascinating study on prayer in the context of romantic relationships. In one study, participants who were currently in an exclusive romantic relationship were recruited. One group of participants was randomly assigned into the prayer condition.

questions.prompt: What were participants in the other group asked to do each day?
questions.promptZh: 另一组参与者每天被要求做什么？
options: Recall their own activities from that day for a while.
Pray for their partner's well-being at least once.
Report four weeks of infidelity before any daily activity.
Repeat their partner's favourite childhood story aloud.
optionsZh: 花些时间回想自己当天做了什么。
至少一次为伴侣福祉祈祷。
在任何每日活动前报告四周的不忠。
大声重述伴侣最喜欢的童年故事。
analyses: A what they had done that day指自己当天所做；each day说明频率。
B 把祈祷组的要求移给了the other group。
C 四周后才报告结果，且该句说日常回想任务而非事前报告。
D 共同讲故事是不同段落的例子，不是控制条件指令。

vocabulary.meaning: 只是；要求限于所述活动
vocabulary.context: 在此说明另一组仅需每日反思当天活动，不带为伴侣祈祷的指定内容。
vocabulary.example: The comparison group was simply asked to reflect on the day.

questions.evidenceQuote: In this condition, they were asked to pray at least once a day for the well-being of their partner for four weeks. The other group was simply asked to take some time each day to think about what they had done that day. Four weeks later, they all reported whether they had engaged in infidelity as well as on their level of relationship satisfaction. Those randomly assigned to the prayer condition were less likely to engage in infidelity than those in the control condition.

questions.prompt: How does telling the same stories fit the preceding discussion?
questions.promptZh: 反复讲同样故事怎样衔接前面的论述？
options: It proves that shared history is absent from marital love.
It establishes that first love always includes more shared history than marriage.
It illustrates how couples revisit a history of shared experiences.
It shows that every retelling must introduce an entirely new event.
optionsZh: 证明婚姻之爱没有共同历史。
确立初恋总比婚姻拥有更多共同历史。
例示伴侣怎样重访共同经历的历史。
说明每次重讲必须引入全新事件。
analyses: A 前句正把shared history作为婚姻之爱的一项特点。
B marital love has but first love lacks的对照方向相反。
C same stories具体体现remembrance of shared experiences；这是本段用例的作用。
D same stories强调回顾同一往事，非每次都是新事件。

vocabulary.meaning: 回忆；对过去经历的记忆
vocabulary.context: 当前指共同经历的历史性，不是对未来计划的预测。
vocabulary.example: Retelling a family story can be an act of remembrance.
collocations: tell each other the same stories

questions.evidenceQuote: In Either/Or, B also argues that the element of history, or the remembrance of shared experiences, is something that marital love has but first love lacks: “The historical nature of marital love is apparent from its being a process of assimilation; it tries its hand in what it experiences and refers its experience back to itself…love emerges tested and purified from this movement and assimilates the experience.” Couples often tell each other the same stories.

questions.prompt: Which detail identifies the Halloween story the author and his wife retell?
questions.promptZh: 哪项细节能准确识别作者夫妇常讲的万圣节往事？
options: Their first son made a chimney hat for his father at university.
Their daughter dressed as a train when she was thirteen.
Their son wore a costume his university classmates had made.
Their first son dressed as Thomas the Tank Engine at age three.
optionsZh: 大儿子在大学给父亲做烟囱帽。
女儿十三岁时扮火车。
儿子穿大学同学做的服装。
大儿子三岁时装扮Thomas the Tank Engine。
analyses: A 烟囱帽由作者做；把制造者、受益者与地点错配。
B first son与three都被改动。
C 服装由妻子制作，未提大学同学制作。
D first son、Thomas、three years old在目标句逐项对应；这是一段个人回忆。

vocabulary.meaning: 复述；把熟悉内容再次讲出来
vocabulary.context: 这里是夫妇重讲往事，不必限定为背诵诗歌或完全逐字不差。
vocabulary.example: They often recite the story of their son's Halloween costume.
collocations: dressed as Thomas the Tank Engine

questions.evidenceQuote: My wife and I often recite a Halloween story about when our first son dressed as Thomas the Tank Engine when he was three years old. My wife made a Thomas costume, a cardboard train decorated with blue felt fabric and yellow and red tape, while I made a chimney-shaped hat. He looked super cute. We brought him to UVA’s big Halloween trick-or-treat on the university’s grounds.

questions.prompt: Who does 'He' refer to in the comment about looking cute?
questions.promptZh: 关于可爱外观的评论里，He指谁？
options: The narrator making the hat.
The first son wearing the Thomas costume.
A university researcher observing the family.
B, the speaker quoted from Either/Or.
optionsZh: 做帽子的叙述者。
穿Thomas服装的大儿子。
观察家庭的大学研究者。
《Either/Or》中被引述的B。
analyses: A 虽上一句有I，当前被描述外观的是穿好服装的孩子。
B My wife made...while I made...后He承接故事里的三岁大儿子，super cute为父亲评价。
C 片段没有观察家庭的研究者。
D B的哲学引述不属于当前万圣节故事的人物。

vocabulary.meaning: 非常；用来强化程度
vocabulary.context: 此处作口语化程度副词修饰cute，非supervisor等名词的缩写。
vocabulary.example: The child looked super cute in the handmade costume.

questions.evidenceQuote: My wife and I often recite a Halloween story about when our first son dressed as Thomas the Tank Engine when he was three years old. My wife made a Thomas costume, a cardboard train decorated with blue felt fabric and yellow and red tape, while I made a chimney-shaped hat. He looked super cute. We brought him to UVA’s big Halloween trick-or-treat on the university’s grounds.

questions.prompt: Where did the family take their son for the Halloween event?
questions.promptZh: 这家人带儿子去哪里参加万圣节活动？
options: To the railway workshop where Thomas costumes were manufactured.
To B's retirement home for a private family dinner.
To a large trick-or-treat event on UVA's university grounds.
To the narrator's high school for a study of relationship quality.
optionsZh: 去生产Thomas服装的铁路车间。
去B的退休住处吃私人家宴。
去UVA校园的大型不给糖就捣蛋活动。
去叙述者高中参加关系质量研究。
analyses: A 火车是服装形象，不能因此改作铁路车间地点。
B B是另一讨论中的人物，并未参与家庭晚宴。
C UVA’s...on the university’s grounds明确地点，big修饰活动规模。
D 高中与实验是其他论述，不能混进本次回忆的活动地点。

vocabulary.meaning: 场地；建筑周围所属的园地
vocabulary.context: the university’s grounds这里是校园场地，不是理由、根据或咖啡渣。
vocabulary.example: The Halloween event took place on the university's grounds.

questions.evidenceQuote: My wife and I often recite a Halloween story about when our first son dressed as Thomas the Tank Engine when he was three years old. My wife made a Thomas costume, a cardboard train decorated with blue felt fabric and yellow and red tape, while I made a chimney-shaped hat. He looked super cute. We brought him to UVA’s big Halloween trick-or-treat on the university’s grounds.

questions.prompt: What does 'fellowship' concern in B's discussion?
questions.promptZh: B的讨论中，fellowship涉及什么？
options: Companionship growing through shared experience over time.
A research grant awarded to the couples after four weeks.
Only the first thrill before any shared history exists.
The elimination of every memory of adversity from marriage.
optionsZh: 随时间在共同经历中形成的情谊。
四周后给伴侣的研究资助。
仅指尚无共同历史时的初次兴奋。
从婚姻中消除所有逆境记忆。
analyses: A development与后文repeated shared experiences over an extended period共同解释这里的情谊。
B fellowship虽可指研究员资助，本段对象是婚姻情谊而非拨款。
C 只初次兴奋与长时间反复共同经历不符。
D shared memory of adversity被纳入婚姻之爱，非要求消除。

vocabulary.meaning: 情谊；共同经历中的伙伴纽带
vocabulary.context: 此处用在婚姻与共同生活，不是学术奖学金或研究员职位的义项。
vocabulary.example: Their fellowship deepened through years of shared experience.

questions.evidenceQuote: B talks about the development of fellowship in Either/Or. Marital love is not just passion and thrill, but also shared memory of adversity. Fellowship emerges out of repeated shared experiences over an extended period of time. Couples who have children can bond over parenthood and learn something new from raising them.

questions.prompt: What does 'not just ... but also' add to the description of marital love?
questions.promptZh: not just...but also给婚姻之爱的描述添加什么？
options: It says passion must disappear before adversity can be remembered.
It confines love to excitement and excludes shared difficulties.
It treats adversity as proof that no companionship exists.
It includes remembered hardship alongside passion and excitement.
optionsZh: 说必须先失去激情才能记得逆境。
把爱限于兴奋，排除共同困难。
把逆境视作无情谊的证据。
在激情与兴奋之外，还纳入共同的困难记忆。
analyses: A not just增加内容，并未设激情先消失的顺序条件。
B but also shared memory of adversity正扩大描述范围。
C 逆境记忆是共同历史的一部分，本句未把它当关系失败的充分证明。
D 并列保留passion/thrill，同时增加shared memory，不能将增加项误读为替代一切。

vocabulary.meaning: 逆境；困难或不利境遇
vocabulary.context: 这里指伴侣共同经历并记得的困难，不等于当下必然处于失败关系。
vocabulary.example: The couple remembered how they had faced adversity together.

questions.evidenceQuote: B talks about the development of fellowship in Either/Or. Marital love is not just passion and thrill, but also shared memory of adversity. Fellowship emerges out of repeated shared experiences over an extended period of time. Couples who have children can bond over parenthood and learn something new from raising them.

questions.prompt: What possibility does the sentence about parenthood describe?
questions.promptZh: 关于育儿的句子描述什么可能？
options: Having children is a necessary condition for every lasting relationship.
Couples with children can strengthen a bond and learn through raising them.
Parenthood guarantees identical experiences for all couples.
Learning about children requires abandoning the bond between partners.
optionsZh: 生孩子是每段长久关系的必要条件。
有孩子的伴侣可在养育中增进纽带并学习。
为人父母保证每对伴侣经历完全一样。
学习育儿必须放弃伴侣之间的纽带。
analyses: A who have children限定所谈群体，未规定所有伴侣必须生育。
B can bond...and learn给可能的纽带与学习机会，没有作普遍保证。
C can不能改为guarantees；也无人人经历相同。
D bond over parenthood正把共同育儿与联系结合，非要求舍弃关系。

vocabulary.meaning: 建立或加深情感纽带
vocabulary.context: 这里是动词，over后接共同经历的育儿，不是购买债券或化学键的名词义。
vocabulary.example: The partners can bond over the experience of parenthood.
collocations: learn something new from raising them

questions.evidenceQuote: B talks about the development of fellowship in Either/Or. Marital love is not just passion and thrill, but also shared memory of adversity. Fellowship emerges out of repeated shared experiences over an extended period of time. Couples who have children can bond over parenthood and learn something new from raising them.

questions.prompt: How does B connect children with understanding one's own life?
questions.promptZh: B怎样把孩子与理解自己人生联系起来？
options: Children supply independent measurements proving that every parental memory is exact.
Only a child's life matters, so a parent's own experience has no relevance.
Every event in a parent's past must occur identically in the child's future.
Life is described as being lived again through children, opening some understanding of one's own life.
optionsZh: 孩子提供独立测量，证明父母所有记忆精确。
只有孩子人生重要，父母经历毫不相关。
父母过去每件事都必须在孩子未来原样发生。
将人生描述为在孩子身上重活，由此获得对自己人生的某些理解。
analyses: A 哲学引语并非独立测量记忆准确率的实验。
B one’s own life正是理解对象，不能删去。
C lived again是引述中的比喻，后文还说similarities and differences。
D lived again与some understanding对应；some保留理解程度，不扩大为通晓全部人生。

vocabulary.meaning: 一些理解；部分领会
vocabulary.context: some限定程度，B的说法没有声称父母因此获得完整无误的人生知识。
vocabulary.example: The experience may bring some understanding of one's own life.

questions.evidenceQuote: As B says, “The whole of life is lived again in the children; only then does one come to some understanding of one’s own life.” When your kids go to elementary school, you will reexperience your elementary school days from a parental perspective. When they go to high school, you will reexperience being in high school, noticing both similarities and differences. B uses poetic reproduction of music as a metaphor for marital love: “In music an even tempo may have much beauty and great effect”—even if it is monotonic.

questions.prompt: What does the high-school example emphasise about reexperiencing the past?
questions.promptZh: 中学的例子强调重历过去时的什么特点？
options: Parents encounter echoes of their own schooling while noticing differences as well.
Parents return as pupils to exactly the same school and year.
Children's schooling removes every difference from the parents' earlier experience.
Only differences can be noticed, because all similarities are excluded.
optionsZh: 父母感受到自己求学经历的回响，同时也看到差异。
父母以学生身份回到完全相同学校和年份。
孩子求学消除了与父母当年的一切差异。
只能见到差异，因为排除了所有相似。
analyses: A reexperience承接parental perspective，both similarities and differences同时保留两面。
B 是从家长视角重体会，不是时空上回到同一年当学生。
C differences明确存在，不能消除。
D both也包括similarities，不能只留一端。

vocabulary.meaning: 重新体验；在新情境中再次感受旧经历
vocabulary.context: 此处从育儿视角感受自己上学时光，不是原样复制每件旧事。
vocabulary.example: Watching a child start school can make a parent reexperience school life.

questions.evidenceQuote: As B says, “The whole of life is lived again in the children; only then does one come to some understanding of one’s own life.” When your kids go to elementary school, you will reexperience your elementary school days from a parental perspective. When they go to high school, you will reexperience being in high school, noticing both similarities and differences. B uses poetic reproduction of music as a metaphor for marital love: “In music an even tempo may have much beauty and great effect”—even if it is monotonic.

questions.prompt: Why is an even musical tempo mentioned?
questions.promptZh: 为什么提到均匀的音乐节奏？
options: To report an experiment proving that monotonous music repairs every marriage.
To prescribe the exact song all married couples must hear daily.
To suggest by metaphor that regularity in marital love can still have beauty and effect.
To show that B rejects any beauty in repeated patterns.
optionsZh: 报告一项证明单调音乐修复每段婚姻的实验。
规定所有伴侣每天必听的确切歌曲。
借比喻说明婚姻之爱的规律性仍可有美感和效果。
说明B否定重复模式的一切美感。
analyses: A metaphor是表达方式，不是音乐干预的实验报告。
B 未规定歌曲、每日频率或人人义务。
C even tempo、may have beauty对应婚姻的规律与重复，保留may的可能。
D 引语肯定均匀节奏可美，非排斥重复。

vocabulary.meaning: 均匀的；稳定一致的
vocabulary.context: 这里修饰tempo，不能读成偶数、甚至或比赛平局。
vocabulary.example: An even tempo can create beauty without constant changes of pace.

questions.evidenceQuote: As B says, “The whole of life is lived again in the children; only then does one come to some understanding of one’s own life.” When your kids go to elementary school, you will reexperience your elementary school days from a parental perspective. When they go to high school, you will reexperience being in high school, noticing both similarities and differences. B uses poetic reproduction of music as a metaphor for marital love: “In music an even tempo may have much beauty and great effect”—even if it is monotonic.

questions.prompt: How is the opening claim about marital monotony qualified?
questions.promptZh: 开头关于婚姻单调的判断有什么限定？
options: Every person is said to find monotony beautiful in the same way.
Monotony can be beautiful, a possibility associated with B's view.
Only unmarried people can perceive beauty in repetition.
The sentence reports a measured improvement caused by monotonous routines.
optionsZh: 说每个人都以同样方式认为单调美好。
单调可以美好，这一可能与B的看法相连。
只有未婚者能从重复中感受美。
报告单调惯例造成可测量的改善。
analyses: A can表示可能，未作所有人一致判断。
B can be beautiful与as...B suggests既保留程度也标出观点出处。
C 本句讨论marital monotony，没有only unmarried的排除。
D suggests的观点引入不等于测量性实验结论。

vocabulary.meaning: 单调；缺少变化的重复状态
vocabulary.context: 此处可被欣赏或觉得无聊，词本身并不决定每个人都持同一评价。
vocabulary.example: The passage considers whether marital monotony can be beautiful.

questions.evidenceQuote: Marital monotony can be beautiful, as Kierkegaard’s B suggests. But for most, like Kierkegaard’s A, it can also be boring. How can we continue to rejuvenate our long-term romantic relationships, beyond prayer? Art Aron and colleagues conducted one of the most famous relationship experiments, which can help us answer this question.

questions.prompt: What does the sentence beginning with 'But' add?
questions.promptZh: 以But开头的句子补充什么？
options: It confirms that A and B must have exactly the same response to monotony.
It says beauty is logically impossible wherever repetition occurs.
It restricts boredom to one documented individual and nobody else.
It introduces boredom as another possible response, associated with most people and A.
optionsZh: 确认A、B对单调必有完全相同反应。
说只要重复，美就逻辑上不可能。
把无聊限于一位有记录的人，排除其他人。
引入另一可能反应：多数人像A一样也可能感到无聊。
analyses: A But标出不同回应，非两人完全相同。
B also保留前句可美好的可能，没有逻辑上全盘推翻。
C for most范围超过一人；也不能改成everybody。
D can also be boring增加另一种体验，for most和like A各限定范围与比照。

vocabulary.meaning: 也；增加另一种可能或属性
vocabulary.context: can also在这里让无聊与前句的美感并存于论述，不要求每人在同一时刻两种感受完全相同。
vocabulary.example: A familiar routine can be comforting and can also become boring.

questions.evidenceQuote: Marital monotony can be beautiful, as Kierkegaard’s B suggests. But for most, like Kierkegaard’s A, it can also be boring. How can we continue to rejuvenate our long-term romantic relationships, beyond prayer? Art Aron and colleagues conducted one of the most famous relationship experiments, which can help us answer this question.

questions.prompt: Which description matches how the experiment allocated participants?
questions.promptZh: 哪项符合实验分配参与者的方法？
options: Couples chose whichever condition they expected to enjoy most.
All dating couples entered one condition and all married couples the other.
Dating and married couples were randomly assigned to one of two conditions.
The same couples completed only an interview without being assigned to a task condition.
optionsZh: 伴侣自选预计最享受的条件。
所有约会伴侣一组、所有已婚伴侣另一组。
约会与已婚伴侣被随机分到两个条件之一。
同一批伴侣只访谈，未分配任务条件。
analyses: A randomly assigned不是自选偏好。
B dating and married描述纳入的人群，不是按婚姻状态固定分组。
C one of two conditions与随机分配逐项吻合，不能把条件数改成人数。
D 后面具体任务说明有实验条件，非只有访谈。

vocabulary.meaning: 随机分配；按随机方式安排条件
vocabulary.context: 这里说实验分组方法，不能因此说样本随机代表所有人群。
vocabulary.example: The participating couples were randomly assigned to two task conditions.

questions.evidenceQuote: In the experiment, dating and married couples were randomly assigned into one of two conditions. Those assigned to a “novel-arousing” task condition were instructed to travel the length of several gym mats and back (roughly thirty feet), remaining on their hands and knees at all times and returning to the starting point, where they were to cross over a rolled-up gym mat approximately three feet high. In addition, they were asked to carry a pillow without using hands, arms, or teeth, even while going over the barrier.

questions.prompt: What comparison is reported after the activity?
questions.promptZh: 活动后报告了什么比较结果？
options: The novel-arousing group reported higher relationship quality than the mundane-task group.
The mundane-task group was directly observed to have better lifelong marriages.
The novel-arousing group had already scored higher before any task was assigned.
Both conditions produced identical self-reported relationship quality after the task.
optionsZh: 新奇唤起组自报关系质量高于平常任务组。
直接观察到平常任务组终身婚姻更好。
分组任务开始前，新奇组分数就已经较高。
两条件活动后自报关系质量完全相同。
analyses: A reported、higher...than、after the activity分别给测量方式、方向与时间。
B 当前结果是活动后自报，不是终身婚姻直接观察；方向也倒置。
C after不能换成before，句中未给预先差异。
D significantly higher不是相同，不能抹平组间结果。

vocabulary.meaning: 报告；此处为参与者自报
vocabulary.context: 与后文observed loving gestures区分；该句并未说研究者直接读出全部内心感受。
vocabulary.example: Participants reported higher relationship quality after the novel task.

questions.evidenceQuote: As Aron predicted, couples completing the novel-arousing task reported significantly higher levels of relationship quality than those completing the mundane task after the activity. The researchers then replicated these findings with a new sample of sixty-three married couples. In a final study, the researchers added two discussion tasks before and after the activity. Couples in the novel-arousing task condition not only reported higher levels of relationship quality but also exhibited more loving gestures during the later discussion task than those in the mundane condition.

questions.prompt: What does the number sixty-three refer to?
questions.promptZh: 63这个数字指什么？
options: The number of years each original couple had been married.
The percentage of the original sample that reported infidelity.
The number of people shown each facial image in the brain study.
The number of married couples in a new sample used to replicate the findings.
optionsZh: 原来每对伴侣结婚的年数。
原样本自报不忠的百分比。
脑研究中看每张面孔的人数。
用于复现结果的新样本里已婚伴侣的对数。
analyses: A sample不是婚龄，sixty-three married couples的计量单位是对。
B 这里是样本数量，非百分比，也非前面的祈祷研究。
C 脑影像是另项研究，不能把63移作其人数。
D new sample和replicated说明重新用63对已婚伴侣复现，不是把原样本重新命名。

vocabulary.meaning: 复现；在再次研究中得到相应发现
vocabulary.context: 本句特指使用新样本，不能理解为每对原伴侣恰做63次。
vocabulary.example: The researchers replicated the findings with a new sample of married couples.
collocations: a new sample of sixty-three married couples

questions.evidenceQuote: As Aron predicted, couples completing the novel-arousing task reported significantly higher levels of relationship quality than those completing the mundane task after the activity. The researchers then replicated these findings with a new sample of sixty-three married couples. In a final study, the researchers added two discussion tasks before and after the activity. Couples in the novel-arousing task condition not only reported higher levels of relationship quality but also exhibited more loving gestures during the later discussion task than those in the mundane condition.

questions.prompt: Which wording best preserves the strength of the finding about novel activities?
questions.promptZh: 哪种表述最准确保留新活动发现的力度？
options: Any new activity guarantees permanent passion in every relationship.
Novel and challenging activities could help rekindle love and passion.
The studies found that familiar activities can never be enjoyable.
Only prayer, rather than any new activity, can possibly maintain affection.
optionsZh: 任何新活动保证每段关系永久激情。
新奇而有挑战的活动可能帮助重燃爱与激情。
研究发现熟悉活动绝不可能令人愉悦。
只有祈祷、没有任何新活动，才可能维持感情。
analyses: A could不能扩大为any、every与permanent guarantee。
B could rekindle保留可能与重新点燃的意义，and even passion包括激情。
C 本句没有否定熟悉活动的全部价值。
D 当前句明确说novel and challenging activities，only prayer把别段内容误作排他结论。

vocabulary.meaning: 重新点燃；使感情或兴趣再起
vocabulary.context: 这里是爱与激情的比喻用法，could保留可能，非承诺永久效果。
vocabulary.example: A shared new experience could rekindle interest in a long relationship.

questions.evidenceQuote: Aron and colleagues found that engaging in novel and challenging activities could rekindle love, and even passion. In a separate line of research, they also found that 40 percent of those married over ten years reported being “very intensely in love.” It turns out that it is possible to keep love alive over many years. In another study, the researchers used a neuroimaging technique, showing participants facial images of their partner as well as images of a close friend and a stranger.

questions.prompt: What does the sentence about keeping love alive establish?
questions.promptZh: 关于让爱保持活力的句子确立什么？
options: Every long marriage necessarily retains equally intense love.
Love can only survive if the marriage has lasted fewer than ten years.
Lasting love over many years is possible, without saying it happens in every marriage.
Forty percent of all marriages were experimentally made passionate by the gym task.
optionsZh: 每段长婚姻都必然保留同样强烈的爱。
只有结婚未满十年爱才可存续。
多年维持爱是可能的，并未说每段婚姻都如此。
体操任务在实验中让所有婚姻的40%变得有激情。
analyses: A possible不是必然，更没有同样强度的全员结论。
B 上句另条研究谈married over ten years，与只能不足十年相反。
C it is possible保留存在可能；邻句的自报比例也不代表所有伴侣。
D 40%来自separate line of research，不能与前面体操任务合并为因果成效。

vocabulary.meaning: 可能的；存在做到的可能性
vocabulary.context: 此处不等于必然发生，也不是每段婚姻概率都精确相同的计算。
vocabulary.example: The passage argues that long-lasting love is possible.
collocations: keep love alive over many years

questions.evidenceQuote: Aron and colleagues found that engaging in novel and challenging activities could rekindle love, and even passion. In a separate line of research, they also found that 40 percent of those married over ten years reported being “very intensely in love.” It turns out that it is possible to keep love alive over many years. In another study, the researchers used a neuroimaging technique, showing participants facial images of their partner as well as images of a close friend and a stranger.

questions.prompt: What were participants shown in the neuroimaging study?
questions.promptZh: 神经影像研究向参与者展示了什么？
options: Facial images of their partner, a close friend, and a stranger.
Only their partner's face, with no comparison faces.
Pictures of their children, their old school, and a gym mat.
Three unfamiliar faces selected to replace all personally known people.
optionsZh: 伴侣、亲密朋友和陌生人的面部图像。
只看伴侣面孔，没有比较面孔。
孩子、旧学校和体操垫的图片。
三张陌生面孔，替代所有认识的人。
analyses: A partner、close friend、stranger三类都明确列在此项研究描述里。
B as well as说明还有两类比较对象，不能删去。
C 其他例子中的对象未成为本句的图像清单。
D partner与close friend是认识的人，不能全部变陌生人；本句讲程序，不直接给脑区结果。

vocabulary.meaning: 以及；也包括
vocabulary.context: 在此把朋友、陌生人图像加入伴侣图像，不表示后两类更重要或没有伴侣图像。
vocabulary.example: The study showed a partner's face as well as comparison faces.
collocations: a close friend and a stranger

questions.evidenceQuote: Aron and colleagues found that engaging in novel and challenging activities could rekindle love, and even passion. In a separate line of research, they also found that 40 percent of those married over ten years reported being “very intensely in love.” It turns out that it is possible to keep love alive over many years. In another study, the researchers used a neuroimaging technique, showing participants facial images of their partner as well as images of a close friend and a stranger.

questions.prompt: What does 'In this way' refer to in the account of continuous rejuvenation?
questions.promptZh: 持续更新论述里的In this way指向什么？
options: Removing every opportunity for self-expansion so that routines remain fixed.
Assuming that marital satisfaction declines for one cause only in all cases.
Replacing all shared activity with an identical daily self-rating questionnaire.
Engaging in novel activities that could offer further opportunities for self-expansion.
optionsZh: 消除所有自我扩展机会，使惯例固定。
假定所有满意度下降都只有一个原因。
用完全相同的每日自评表替代所有共同活动。
参与可能提供更多自我扩展机会的新活动。
analyses: A 前句是provide further opportunities，非消除机会。
B due in part只说部分原因，不能改成所有情况唯一成因。
C 当前段没有要求用问卷替代活动。
D this way回指前句的新活动—自我扩展机会；theorizes/could/can保留理论与可能性，并非每段关系必然更新。

vocabulary.meaning: 恢复活力；更新
vocabulary.context: 此处指伴侣关系获得新活力，非生物年龄倒退；can也没有保证永久持续。
vocabulary.example: The theory links shared novelty with opportunities for rejuvenation.

questions.evidenceQuote: Aron theorizes that the typical decline in marital satisfaction over the course of a marriage is due in part to this lack of new opportunities to expand the self, and that engagement in novel activities could provide further opportunities for self-expansion. In this way, couples can experience “continuous rejuvenation.”
